pairs.ask: SIM-Swap Protection: Turn On Your Carrier's Number Lock And Port-Out PIN This Week, Or Later? (fcc.gov SIM swap rules 2023)

optionA.label: Turn On This Week
optionA.desc: Stops someone moving your number to their SIM to grab codes.

optionB.label: Later
optionB.desc: Leaves the phone number open to port-out fraud.

pairs.ask: Phone Number As Account Recovery: Remove It From Google, GitHub And Stripe Recovery, Or Keep It As A Backup?

optionA.label: Remove The Phone Number
optionA.desc: A swapped SIM can no longer reset your accounts.

optionB.label: Keep As Backup
optionB.desc: Easier recovery, but the number becomes a weak spot.

pairs.ask: Google Advanced Protection Program For Your Main Email: Enroll, Or Standard Security? (landing.google.com/advancedprotection)

optionA.label: Enroll
optionA.desc: Strongest Google account protection; needs passkeys or keys.

optionB.label: Standard Security
optionB.desc: Fewer limits on apps and recovery.

pairs.ask: Admin Email For Registrar, Stripe And GitHub: A Separate Unpublished Address, Or Your Public Email?

optionA.label: Separate Unpublished Address
optionA.desc: Attackers cannot target an address they never see.

optionB.label: Public Email
optionB.desc: One inbox; also the one phishers know.

pairs.ask: Domain Registrar Lock (Transfer Lock) On maxweberman.com And smartupkeep.ai: Confirm It Is On, Or Leave Default? (icann.org transfer lock)

optionA.label: Confirm Lock Is On
optionA.desc: Blocks unauthorized transfers away from your registrar.

optionB.label: Leave Default
optionB.desc: Some registrars leave it off.

pairs.ask: Domain Auto-Renew Plus A Backup Card And Expiry Alerts: Set Up, Or Renew Manually?

optionA.label: Auto-Renew With Backup Card
optionA.desc: Lapsed domains get grabbed and used for phishing.

optionB.label: Renew Manually
optionB.desc: Relies on remembering every date.

pairs.ask: CAA DNS Records: Limit Which Companies Can Issue Certificates For Your Domains, Or Allow Any? (RFC 8659)

optionA.label: Add CAA Records
optionA.desc: Only your chosen certificate issuers can make certs for your sites.

optionB.label: Allow Any
optionB.desc: Default; any certificate authority can issue.

pairs.ask: Email Spoofing: Publish SPF, DKIM And DMARC (p=reject) For Your Domains, Or Leave It? (Google sender guidelines)

optionA.label: Set Up DMARC Reject
optionA.desc: Stops others sending email that looks like it is from you.

optionB.label: Leave It
optionB.desc: Your domain can be spoofed to customers.

pairs.ask: Contractor Offboarding: Same-Day Checklist To Remove GitHub, Drive, Dropbox And Tool Access, Or Ad Hoc?

optionA.label: Same-Day Checklist
optionA.desc: Ex-helpers lose access the day work ends.

optionB.label: Ad Hoc
optionB.desc: Old access tends to linger for months.

pairs.ask: Shared Logins: One Seat Per Person (Or Shared Vault Items), Or Share Passwords In Chat?

optionA.label: One Seat Or Vault Sharing
optionA.desc: You can remove one person without changing everyone's password.

optionB.label: Share In Chat
optionB.desc: Passwords live forever in chat history.

pairs.ask: Tool Inventory: One List Of Every Service, Its Owner And Its Login Method, Or Keep It In Your Head? (CISA Cyber Essentials)

optionA.label: Keep One List
optionA.desc: Makes offboarding, billing and incidents much faster.

optionB.label: In Your Head
optionB.desc: Easy now, hard in an emergency.

pairs.ask: Connected Apps Review: Remove Unused Apps With Access To Google And GitHub Every Quarter, Or Never?

optionA.label: Quarterly Review
optionA.desc: Old connected apps are a quiet way in.

optionB.label: Never
optionB.desc: Access keeps piling up.

pairs.ask: Restore Drill: Actually Restore One Repo And One Dropbox Folder Each Quarter, Or Trust The Backups?

optionA.label: Quarterly Restore Drill
optionA.desc: Proves backups work before you need them.

optionB.label: Trust The Backups
optionB.desc: Many backups fail only at restore time.

pairs.ask: Break-Glass Account: One Emergency Admin Login Stored Offline, Or None?

optionA.label: Keep A Break-Glass Login
optionA.desc: A way back in if your main account is locked or taken.

optionB.label: None
optionB.desc: One locked account can stop everything.

pairs.ask: Business Continuity: Set Google Inactive Account Manager And Name A Trusted Contact, Or Skip?

optionA.label: Set It Up
optionA.desc: Someone you trust can reach key accounts if you cannot.

optionB.label: Skip
optionB.desc: Accounts could be stranded.

pairs.ask: Agent Identity: Give Agents Their Own Bot GitHub Account Or GitHub App, Or Let Them Use Your Account?

optionA.label: Separate Bot Identity
optionA.desc: Agent actions are clearly separate and easy to revoke.

optionB.label: Your Account
optionB.desc: Agents can do anything you can.

pairs.ask: Agent Sandbox: Agents Only Work On The Shared Box, Never In Your Personal Browser Sessions, Or Allow Both?

optionA.label: Box Only
optionA.desc: Your personal logins stay out of agent reach.

optionB.label: Allow Both
optionB.desc: More convenient, much more exposure.

pairs.ask: Agent Secrets: Keep Keys In A Secrets Manager Or Env Store, Or In Files Inside Repos?

optionA.label: Secrets Manager
optionA.desc: Keys never land in a repo by accident.

optionB.label: Files In Repos
optionB.desc: Easy to leak in a commit.

pairs.ask: Agent Action Log: Keep A 90-Day Log Of What Agents Ran And Changed, Or No Log?

optionA.label: Keep A 90-Day Log
optionA.desc: You can see what happened after a bad change.

optionB.label: No Log
optionB.desc: Hard to trace mistakes.

pairs.ask: Payment Change Requests: Always Confirm By A Known Phone Number Before Changing Where Money Goes, Or Trust Email? (FBI IC3 business email compromise)

optionA.label: Call To Confirm
optionA.desc: Stops the most common business email fraud.

optionB.label: Trust Email
optionB.desc: Fake invoices and bank changes get through.
